intended_object: The standard Frobenius endomorphism F_p of the symplectic group Sp_{2(n+1)}(F̄_p) attached to a type-C Lie-type index: the map that raises every matrix entry to the p-th power, where p is the defining characteristic. Inferred from the docstring and the companion lemmas `coe_primeFrobenius_apply` and `frobenius_eq_primeFrobenius_pow`.
explanation:
The definition is `SpStd.frobenius d.carrierRank p 1 d.1.Closure`. `SpStd.frobenius n p k A` is the map on the points of the standard symplectic carrier that comes from functoriality applied to `iterateFrobenius A p k`. With k = 1 this is the ring Frobenius x ↦ x^p, applied entrywise. Here the ring is `d.1.Closure`, the algebraic closure of the prime field, and `p` is the index's characteristic. So the definition gives the entrywise p-power Frobenius on Sp(F̄_p), and the lemma `coe_primeFrobenius_apply` confirms that it raises each entry to the p-th power. That is exactly the standard prime-field Frobenius of the classical symplectic group, as the docstring says.

The object is specific: one particular endomorphism of the ambient group attached to the index. The general construction, for any ring of exponential characteristic p and any exponent k, already exists in the library as `SpStd.frobenius`. This definition only specialises it to the index's data, so it is not too narrow.

Mathlib has the ring Frobenius (`frobenius`, `iterateFrobenius`) and `Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.map`. It has no Frobenius endomorphism of symplectic groups as a named declaration, so there is no Mathlib counterpart.
